answer.rationale: Primary contract is 14 days from hard expiry with the line at 94% and no buffer, so any action that adds onboarding or coverage gap raises delivery risk and violates the TCO-without-more-risk objective. The low-cost quote is a useful mandate-meeting benchmark, but last year's clean switch (c2) is a different operating condition and is not sufficient to justify moving primary supply under current utilization. Incumbent renewal historically protected integration and deliveries (c1); renegotiation at renewal previously moved price and terms when market-benchmarked (c4). Intend to use the competing quote to press the incumbent rather than switch, renew passively, dual-source, or defer a non-auto-renewing primary. Verifying c2 and c4 before treating those lessons as load-bearing; whether the incumbent can actually close an 18% gap remains unknown.
